definitions: Sound whose source is visible on the screen or whose source is implied to be present by the action of the film.
Sound that originates from a source within the narrative world of a film or play, audible to both the characters and the audience.
examples: The characters in the film can hear the diegetic sound.
Music coming from a radio within the scene is an example of diegetic sound.
Footsteps and dialogue are typically diegetic sound.
